wnba.null_arm_demonstration: CHALLENGER and BASELINE return byte-identical metrics, as they must: the challenger IS the baseline on this sport. That is the negative control behaving exactly as a negative control should, and it is the reason it cannot count as challenger coverage.

THE_OWNER_QUESTION.asked: whether the prior-heavy challenger improves calibration while sacrificing discrimination
THE_OWNER_QUESTION.descriptive_answer: On this slate it did the OPPOSITE of the feared failure mode. Discrimination went UP, not down: AUC 0.660 challenger vs 0.580 champion vs 0.500 baseline. Calibration is the half that failed — the challenger's calibration slope is 5.86, meaning the outcomes moved about six times as much as its forecasts did. It compressed, and it compressed far too much.
THE_OWNER_QUESTION.so_the_diagnosis_inverts: the challenger has ordering skill its probabilities do not express. That is a fixable defect (the offset is over-regularised) and a different problem from the one the compression statistic suggested.
THE_OWNER_QUESTION.caveat: n=15 on one night, and a calibration line fitted across a 12pp forecast range. The slope is NUMERICALLY_ESTIMABLE under the Hessian rule and is still not evidence of anything at this sample size. calibration_acceptable is FALSE for both fitted arms, separately from estimability, exactly as the two rules are meant to separate.

WHAT_ACTUALLY_MATTERS_MOST.finding: THE EXPANDING TOTAL PRIOR BEAT EVERY MODEL ARM ON TOTALS.
WHAT_ACTUALLY_MATTERS_MOST.why_it_matters: the card's BASELINE total was the CHALLENGER's total, so the card as shipped had no comparator at all on this estimand and this result was invisible. The comparator added under amendment 3 — a single league-mean number, 8.984 runs, that knows nothing about the teams — is the most accurate total on the board. Lesson 20 arriving on schedule: check the base rate before crediting the model.
WHAT_ACTUALLY_MATTERS_MOST.direction: all four are negatively biased (signed −0.42 to −0.71): every arm under-projected scoring, and CHC 19-2 supplies the largest miss in each.

CHAMPION_READ: 9-6, Brier skill +0.00076 over the prior. That is three orders of magnitude below the challenger's and is indistinguishable from zero at any sample size. The frozen V13 arm added essentially nothing over a single league-average number on this slate.
WNBA_READ: the champion went 4-0 with Brier skill +0.568 and AUC 1.0 — on FOUR games, every one of them action-blocked for a feature state 32 days stale against a 21-day ceiling. Four Bernoulli trials cannot distinguish a good model from a lucky one, and a perfect AUC on n=4 occurs by chance about 4% of the time under a coin flip. The correct reading is 'not evaluable and interesting', not 'the stale arm was right all along'. The CHALLENGER returns byte-identical numbers to the BASELINE, as a negative control must.
NFL_READ: one game, one arm, home won. Reported so it is not silently dropped, not because it means anything.
